criteria.evidence: One clear central idea: the instinctive, fluid gesture of detaching the neck-worn battery to rescue a dying phone in real time.
criteria.refinement: Ensure the motion reads as reflexive, not choreographed—use subtle motion blur only on background, not product.

criteria.evidence: Directly addresses active urban users, urgent need, verified features (screen, strap, cable), and avoids generic travel tropes or decorative backdrops.
criteria.refinement: Anchor the setting in a non-iconic, functional urban micro-scene (e.g. tram stop, bike lane edge) to avoid tourist cliché.

criteria.evidence: Evokes calm competence and relief—not panic—aligning with the brief’s ‘discreet but concrete’ emotional register for active-day vulnerability.
criteria.refinement: Avoid smiling or exaggerated expressions; keep facial neutrality to emphasize action over emotion.

criteria.evidence: Product is hero: the entire narrative hinges on its unique neck-worn deployment, visible screen, and integrated cable—no story without it.
criteria.refinement: Ensure the unclipping mechanism is visible but not over-explained; the gesture implies function.

criteria.evidence: Only this product combines neck strap, digital display, and integrated cable into a single rescue gesture—no competitor can replicate the action authentically.
criteria.refinement: Highlight matte black finish against motion-blurred background to reinforce material authenticity.

criteria.evidence: Uses real product photo, deterministic scene (urban street mid-stride), readable screen (78% visible), and clear typography placement possible in 4:5 format.
criteria.refinement: Test screen legibility at 15% image height; ensure USB-C plug end is visible when extended.

criteria.evidence: Product is dominant and recognizable, but price/claim placement must be ensured in layout; current concept doesn’t specify typographic integration.
criteria.refinement: Reserve bottom third for clean price + claim block without competing with gesture focal point.

criteria.evidence: Idea (instinctive rescue), metaphor (pendant of readiness), and story (vulnerability → competence) align tightly around one moment.
criteria.refinement: Ensure the phone’s red-low-battery icon is subtly visible to complete the cause-effect loop.

criteria.evidence: Avoids stock travel imagery; the neck-detach gesture is specific to this product’s form and use case, not a template trope.
criteria.refinement: Reject any background elements that read as ‘city aesthetic’ (e.g. graffiti walls, iconic bridges).

criteria.evidence: Strong visual (compass metaphor) but risks abstraction—the ‘directional instrument’ idea requires interpretation, not instant grasp.
criteria.refinement: Replace compass framing with direct user glance at screen while walking; keep cable unfurling as proof of readiness.

criteria.evidence: Addresses verified features but leans into intellectual metaphor over urgent utility; brief demands ‘instinctive action’, not contemplation.
criteria.refinement: Shift from static pavement shot to mid-motion step where user checks screen *while moving*, reinforcing active context.

criteria.evidence: ‘Measured control’ fits premium restraint, but feels detached from the high-stakes urgency of a dying phone in active use.
criteria.refinement: Add subtle tension: phone screen flickering amber in periphery, user’s pace unchanged—confidence through preparedness.

criteria.evidence: Battery’s screen and cable are central to the metaphor; the ‘directional’ reading only works because of numeric display and integrated cable.
criteria.refinement: Ensure screen shows exact % (e.g. 42%)—not symbolic icons—to ground metaphor in verified fact.

criteria.evidence: The combo of screen + cable + neck strap is unique, but ‘compass’ framing is a known visual trope that could be reused generically.
criteria.refinement: Abandon compass analogy; instead show battery held palm-up as user glances at it mid-stride—more authentic, less stylized.

criteria.evidence: Sun-dappled pavement risks glare on screen; digital display must remain legible under variable light without post-processing.
criteria.refinement: Use overcast daylight or shaded alley lighting to guarantee screen visibility without retouching.

criteria.evidence: Product is visible but framed as an object of contemplation, not action—risk of downplaying urgency that drives store visit.
criteria.refinement: Integrate price/claim near battery’s base, using same matte-black-on-light contrast as product finish.

criteria.evidence: Metaphor (compass) and story (checking charge) connect, but the ‘time passage via shadows’ adds a second layer that dilutes the core action.
criteria.refinement: Remove shadow-time motif; focus solely on user’s glance → screen → continued movement.

criteria.evidence: Sun-dappled pavement + held-object composition resembles stock ‘mindfulness tech’ imagery; lacks the urgent, physical specificity of the brief.
criteria.refinement: Replace serene pavement with dynamic urban transition zone (e.g. crossing street, entering metro turnstile) to force action context.

criteria.evidence: Single powerful idea: silent power exchange via pre-connected battery, emphasizing zero-friction sharing enabled by integrated design.
criteria.refinement: Ensure both hands are equally lit and positioned to avoid implying donation vs. mutual aid.

criteria.evidence: Centers verified features (integrated cable, neck strap, 100% screen) in a real-use scenario (friend’s dead phone), avoiding generic gift or solo travel tropes.
criteria.refinement: Specify both users are mid-activity (e.g. cycling, walking with bags) to reinforce ‘active day’ context.

criteria.evidence: ‘Shared resilience’ fits relationship-building, but risks sentimentality if hands are too posed; brief asks for ‘discreet relief’, not warmth.
criteria.refinement: Keep faces out of frame; focus on hands, cable connection, and screen—emotion conveyed through efficiency, not expression.

criteria.evidence: Battery is the tool enabling the exchange; its neck strap explains why it’s instantly available, and screen confirms readiness—no substitute possible.
criteria.refinement: Show cordon attachment point clearly between hands to prove neck-worn origin without showing full body.

criteria.evidence: Only this model allows plug-and-play sharing without fumbling for cables or cases—gesture is physically impossible with other power banks.
criteria.refinement: Emphasize the click of connection and cable tension to signal immediacy and reliability.

criteria.evidence: Real product, deterministic handshake composition, readable 100% screen, and 4:5 framing allow clean typography placement below hands.
criteria.refinement: Use shallow depth of field to blur background but keep cable plug and screen in sharp focus.

criteria.evidence: Product is central and active; price/claim can occupy lower third without disrupting the hand-to-hand power transfer focal point.
criteria.refinement: Place price left-aligned, claim right-aligned beneath hands—minimal, high-contrast, no decorative fonts.

criteria.evidence: Idea (silent exchange), metaphor (handshake of reliability), and story (mid-conversation rescue) form a tight, causal chain.
criteria.refinement: Ensure phone screen is off or red-low-battery visible to justify urgency without text.

criteria.evidence: No stock gestures or backdrops; the neck-to-hand transfer is unique to this product’s form factor and use case.
criteria.refinement: Avoid any background signage, logos, or recognizable landmarks—keep environment neutral but textured (e.g. concrete wall, metal railing).
